h1:
Pai vs Chiang Rai
which to choose?
intro: Torn between Pai and Chiang Rai? Here is an honest, side-by-side comparison so you can pick the one that fits your trip — or fit both in.

blocks.html: Short answer: Both are northern add-ons beyond Chiang Mai. Choose Pai for a small, chilled, bohemian mountain town — cafés, hot springs, sea of mist (west, ~3h over 762 curves). Choose Chiang Rai for a larger town with clear-cut sights — the White and Blue Temples, tea plantations and mountains (north, ~3h).

blocks.text: Pai vs Chiang Rai at a glance

items: Pick Pai if you want a chilled mountain town with cafés, hot springs and mist, and do not need lots of sights
Pick Chiang Rai if you want clear attractions like the White Temple, tea farms and mountains
With time, do both — both extend from Chiang Mai; do Pai (west) first, then loop to Chiang Rai (north)

faq.q: Pai or Chiang Rai — which is better?
faq.a: Pai suits those who want to chill in a small mountain town with cafés and nature and few must-sees, while Chiang Rai is bigger with clear attractions like the White Temple and tea farms. Choose by whether you prefer chilling or ticking off sights.

faq.q: From Chiang Mai, is Pai or Chiang Rai easier to reach?
faq.a: Both take about 3 hours, but the road to Pai has 762 curves so motion-sickness-prone travelers should prepare, while the road to Chiang Rai is smoother with big coaches available.

faq.q: Can I do both Pai and Chiang Rai in one trip?
faq.a: Yes with time — both extend from Chiang Mai but in different directions (Pai west, Chiang Rai north). Most use Chiang Mai as a base and visit each separately rather than going directly between Pai and Chiang Rai.
